name: Governance, ownership and asset inventory
goal: Know what exists, who can authorize changes, and who is accountable for harm.

controls.name: Accountable owners
controls.check: Assign a business owner, technical owner, security owner and responder for every production agent and workflow, including vendor-managed agents.
controls.evidence: Reconcile the registry against running workloads and vendor accounts; retain owner acknowledgments and escalation contacts.
controls.mistake: A platform owner is listed, but nobody owns the actions of individual agents.

controls.name: Complete agent inventory
controls.check: Record agent purpose, environment, model, framework, autonomy mode, identities, tools, inputs, outputs and downstream systems.
controls.evidence: Compare declared inventory with runtime, API gateway, IAM, billing and scheduler observations.
controls.mistake: Shadow agents, scheduled jobs, browser extensions and experimental endpoints remain outside governance.

controls.name: Risk classification
controls.check: Classify workflows by reachable data, maximum action impact, tenant exposure and reversibility; assess combined workflow capability.
controls.evidence: Retain a workflow risk assessment with actual reachable assets and approval requirements.
controls.mistake: A read-only agent receives a low rating even though it can trigger a privileged worker.

controls.name: Permitted business purpose
controls.check: Define allowed tasks, prohibited actions, environment scope and accountable authority for exceptions in enforceable policy.
controls.evidence: Run an allowed task and a same-tool prohibited task; retain both policy decisions.
controls.mistake: A broad objective such as fix production becomes implicit authorization for any action.

controls.name: Vendor responsibility
controls.check: Document who retains traces, rotates identities, suspends execution, restores data and reports incidents for each provider.
controls.evidence: Keep contractual responsibility records and test a support escalation with representative evidence.
controls.mistake: An outsourced model or agent has no usable emergency suspension or log-export route.

controls.name: Change and exception control
controls.check: Version risk acceptance, permission changes, new tools and temporary bypasses; require an owner, expiry and compensating control.
controls.evidence: Sample recent changes and expired exceptions; verify runtime state matches approved records.
controls.mistake: A temporary administrator role or approval bypass silently becomes permanent.

controls.name: Data and dependency catalog
controls.check: Inventory retrieval sources, vector stores, memories, queues, caches, secret stores, plugins, skill packages and model artifacts.
controls.evidence: Trace one real task through all dependencies and reconcile the catalog with observed connections.
controls.mistake: Only the LLM endpoint is documented; persistent state and tool infrastructure are invisible.

controls.name: Assessment freshness
controls.check: Reassess after model, prompt, tool, identity, policy or architecture changes; define evidence validity windows by risk.
controls.evidence: Show a change-triggered assessment and a periodic review; record assessment date and scope.
controls.mistake: A prior passing test is treated as proof for a materially different deployment.

name: Architecture and trust boundaries
goal: Separate facts, instructions and execution authority throughout the complete workflow.

controls.name: End-to-end data-flow map
controls.check: Map user input, external content, agents, delegates, tools, credentials and side effects, labeling every trust boundary.
controls.evidence: Walk a task from ingress to final resource mutation; compare diagram with traces and network paths.
controls.mistake: The design ends at the model response while the dangerous action occurs downstream.

controls.name: Control plane separation
controls.check: Separate deployment configuration, policies, identity provisioning and approval systems from agent-readable task content.
controls.evidence: Attempt configuration writes using normal task identities; inspect authorization and protected storage.
controls.mistake: An agent can rewrite the instructions or allowlist that governs its own actions.

controls.name: Explicit input trust
controls.check: Label retrieved text, tool results, emails, documents and peer messages as data with provenance and permitted uses.
controls.evidence: Inspect a trace containing multiple source types; verify labels survive transforms and handoffs.
controls.mistake: A trusted connector is assumed to make every document it fetches trustworthy.

controls.name: Execution enforcement points
controls.check: Place deterministic authorization before tool effects and at downstream resources; make bypass paths subject to equivalent controls.
controls.evidence: Trace denied calls through gateway and direct routes; confirm no unauthorized state changes.
controls.mistake: A model-side guard is the only barrier while a worker or direct API bypasses it.

controls.name: Transitive capability graph
controls.check: Map invoke, write, deploy, assume-role, credential-read and configuration-edit edges; compute reachable high-impact paths.
controls.evidence: Review paths from each low-trust principal to production writes, IAM changes and external egress.
controls.mistake: Individual roles appear minimal while their composition permits effective administrator activity.

controls.name: Tenant and environment boundaries
controls.check: Bind tenant, user, workflow and environment to task state, retrieval and execution using trusted context.
controls.evidence: Run cross-tenant and development-to-production negative cases; retain resource-side decisions.
controls.mistake: Caller-supplied tenant fields or environment names override authenticated scope.

controls.name: Fail-safe dependency behavior
controls.check: Define safe outcomes when policy, identity, approval, logging or retrieval services fail, including queued work.
controls.evidence: Simulate outages; confirm risky actions stop or use a preapproved degraded mode.
controls.mistake: An unavailable policy service triggers a permissive fallback for business continuity.

controls.name: Alternate execution paths
controls.check: Inventory retries, webhooks, callbacks, batch workers, manual endpoints, debug consoles and vendor background actions.
controls.evidence: Compare enforcement coverage across synchronous and asynchronous paths using the same restricted task.
controls.mistake: The interactive API is secure but the queue consumer trusts old task metadata.

name: Workload identity and effective privilege
goal: Use distinct accountable identities and constrain their effective reach.

controls.name: Distinct workload identities
controls.check: Give agents and tool workers separate identities by role and environment; avoid shared administrator credentials.
controls.evidence: Map each running component to its effective principal and permissions; review shared identity exceptions.
controls.mistake: All agents use one platform account, preventing attribution and granular containment.

controls.name: Least effective privilege
controls.check: Restrict actions, resources, conditions and delegation edges to actual tasks; include ability to mutate code or configuration.
controls.evidence: Combine IAM analysis with controlled negative tests and observed usage over a representative period.
controls.mistake: Read-only data access includes secrets or writable instructions that unlock privileged execution.

controls.name: Originating principal binding
controls.check: Preserve the authenticated user or triggering workload separately from the executing service account in trusted task context.
controls.evidence: Correlate ingress authentication with delegate and tool logs; try forged origin fields.
controls.mistake: Resource audit logs show only high-priv-write-service, hiding who caused the action.

controls.name: No ambient administrator access
controls.check: Remove default cloud credentials, inherited shells, browser profiles and broad instance identities from task runtimes.
controls.evidence: Inspect effective credential resolution and test access to unrelated resources in a disposable environment.
controls.mistake: The intended token is scoped, but SDK fallback discovers a stronger ambient identity.

controls.name: Privilege separation
controls.check: Separate observation, proposal, approval and execution responsibilities; prevent one agent from granting its own authority.
controls.evidence: Show distinct write paths and deny self-approval, role assignment and policy modification.
controls.mistake: Multiple agent names give the appearance of separation while sharing one trust boundary.

controls.name: Human versus service authority
controls.check: Define when actions run on behalf of a user and when a service performs a separately authorized business operation.
controls.evidence: Verify both modes with documented entitlements and decision logs.
controls.mistake: Service credentials silently replace a user's missing permission during delegation.

controls.name: Dynamic privilege review
controls.check: Review inherited groups, role assumptions, federation, managed policies and new tool grants as privileges evolve.
controls.evidence: Capture effective permission snapshots at deployment and after IAM changes; diff privileged edges.
controls.mistake: An external IAM change expands agent reach without any agent configuration change.

controls.name: Identity retirement
controls.check: Remove dormant agents, old deployments, abandoned refresh tokens and orphaned service principals.
controls.evidence: Reconcile workload deletion with IAM and secret-store removal; demonstrate stale access denial.
controls.mistake: A retired agent remains a valid authenticated route into the platform.

name: Credentials, tokens and revocation
goal: Keep credentials outside model context and make credential compromise containable.

controls.name: Credential isolation
controls.check: Inject credentials into trusted execution components rather than prompts, memory or tool descriptions; minimize exposure to agent code.
controls.evidence: Inspect request bodies, traces, error paths and environment access for credential leakage.
controls.mistake: A secret is hidden in normal output but appears in tool errors or debugging traces.

controls.name: Short-lived scoped access
controls.check: Use narrowly scoped, short-lived credentials where supported, with controlled renewal and documented maximum lifetime.
controls.evidence: Inspect token claims or introspection results and renewal policy; test access after expiration.
controls.mistake: A short access-token lifetime is undermined by a long-lived unrestricted refresh token.

controls.name: Audience and issuer validation
controls.check: Validate intended resource, trusted issuer, expiry and required scope at each resource boundary; reject mismatched credentials.
controls.evidence: Present expired, wrong-audience and wrong-issuer test tokens; retain resource-side rejection records.
controls.mistake: A valid signature is treated as enough to authorize use at any service.

controls.name: Delegated token constraints
controls.check: If using token exchange or capabilities, enforce approved subject, actor, audience, actions, resources and expiry in the issuer policy.
controls.evidence: Review issuance rules and test requests for expanded scopes or impersonation.
controls.mistake: Token exchange becomes a privilege minting mechanism because the issuer accepts requested scopes blindly.

controls.name: Secret access boundaries
controls.check: Limit which workloads can read each secret; isolate production, tenant and tool-specific values and rotation authority.
controls.evidence: Use controlled cross-role secret-read tests and inspect vault audit records.
controls.mistake: The agent cannot call a write API directly but can read its administrator token.

controls.name: Revocation coverage
controls.check: Document how to invalidate access tokens, sessions, refresh grants, assumed-role sessions and tool credentials; measure enforcement delays.
controls.evidence: Revoke a test identity and check every gateway, cache, direct API and worker path.
controls.mistake: Deleting a key leaves existing sessions or stateless tokens valid until expiry.

controls.name: Rotation without re-exposure
controls.check: Rotate affected credentials through a trusted control plane; ensure new values are not returned to compromised workloads.
controls.evidence: Demonstrate rotation with agent suspension and verify old credentials fail and new distribution is constrained.
controls.mistake: Rotation immediately hands the replacement secret back to the same compromised agent.

controls.name: Secret leakage detection
controls.check: Scan repositories, task context, traces, memory, output files and exported bundles using restricted access and safe redaction.
controls.evidence: Plant a synthetic credential marker; verify detection and removal from derived stores.
controls.mistake: DLP covers chat responses but misses checkpoint files, backups and third-party trace exports.

name: Delegation and cross-agent authorization
goal: A handoff must preserve authority constraints rather than borrow the receiver's privileges.

controls.name: Authenticated handoffs
controls.check: Authenticate both sender and receiver; accept delegation only through approved channels with authenticated workflow context.
controls.evidence: Try unauthenticated and wrong-workflow handoffs; inspect rejection and identity attribution.
controls.mistake: A peer message says system approved and the receiver treats the text as identity proof.

controls.name: Bounded delegated authority
controls.check: Bind delegation to specific action, resources, tenant, purpose, time and permitted next hop; prevent automatic scope expansion.
controls.evidence: Attempt a broader action and another resource through the same delegate; retain policy denials.
controls.mistake: Agent A requests a harmless task then reuses the handoff for unrestricted writes.

controls.name: Independent receiver authorization
controls.check: Require the privileged receiver and tool boundary to validate authority for the concrete requested operation before effects.
controls.evidence: Send an unauthorized write through low-priv-read-service; confirm denial before tool execution.
controls.mistake: The privileged receiver authorizes its own service account and ignores the caller's limits.

controls.name: Preserved provenance
controls.check: Carry origin identity, parent task, source references, scope and policy version through summaries and nested delegations.
controls.evidence: Reconstruct a multi-hop trace and verify source trust labels survive summarization.
controls.mistake: A summary converts attacker-controlled text into an apparently authoritative instruction.

controls.name: No authority from natural language
controls.check: Keep approvals, roles and delegation grants in validated structured records; treat claims inside task text as untrusted.
controls.evidence: Submit forged approved-by and role claims within content and confirm they cannot change policy.
controls.mistake: The receiver accepts a convincing statement that an administrator approved the action.

controls.name: Depth and fan-out limits
controls.check: Limit delegation depth, parallel branches, spawned identities and total aggregate capability; detect cycles.
controls.evidence: Exercise a bounded cycle and fan-out; verify counters and safe termination across workers.
controls.mistake: Each agent stays under its quota while combined branches create unbounded activity.

controls.name: Replay and substitution resistance
controls.check: Bind grants to task and request identifiers, expiry and payload; prevent reuse or swapping approved parameters.
controls.evidence: Replay a completed grant and alter one parameter; confirm denial without new side effects.
controls.mistake: A signed handoff proves origin but remains reusable or authorizes changed arguments.

controls.name: Service-owned exceptions
controls.check: For a privileged business service, define an explicit operation contract, bounded entitlement and approval instead of assuming caller privilege intersection.
controls.evidence: Test both a legitimate low-privilege request and a forbidden variant; retain the separate service-policy decision.
controls.mistake: A strict intersection breaks intended services, so teams disable checks entirely instead of defining bounded delegation.

name: Tool and MCP integration security
goal: Treat tools as independently secured services with real authorization and observable side effects.

controls.name: Approved server registry
controls.check: Allow only vetted tool and MCP servers, exact endpoints and versioned packages; verify identity before connection.
controls.evidence: Compare runtime tool discovery with approved registry and test an unregistered endpoint.
controls.mistake: Dynamic discovery adds a malicious server without security review.

controls.name: Tool capability contracts
controls.check: Document actual effects, resources, required roles and risk for each tool; treat read-only or safe annotations as advisory.
controls.evidence: Inspect implementation and exercise effects against disposable targets; compare with declared contract.
controls.mistake: A tool labeled read-only creates exports, invokes webhooks or writes temporary files.

controls.name: Server-side authorization
controls.check: Enforce per-operation resource and tenant authorization inside the tool service even when gateway checks pass.
controls.evidence: Call the server directly and through the agent with insufficient scope; verify both deny.
controls.mistake: Tool access authentication is mistaken for authorization to every operation it exposes.

controls.name: Schema and semantic validation
controls.check: Validate argument types, ranges, paths, destinations, resource identifiers and business constraints outside the model.
controls.evidence: Submit malformed and well-formed-but-forbidden arguments; inspect validation failures.
controls.mistake: JSON schema passes while a valid URL or identifier points to a forbidden resource.

controls.name: MCP transport and sessions
controls.check: Apply authorization suited to the deployed transport; bind sessions to authenticated principals and validate every protected request.
controls.evidence: Review HTTP authorization and local process credentials separately; test session reuse across users.
controls.mistake: A session identifier is accepted as authentication, or local stdio inherits excessive environment credentials.

controls.name: OAuth and upstream separation
controls.check: Validate token audiences; avoid token passthrough; separate upstream credentials and preserve per-client consent in proxy flows.
controls.evidence: Test wrong-audience tokens and independent client consent; review callback and token storage controls.
controls.mistake: A proxy forwards caller tokens blindly or shares one user's upstream consent across clients.

controls.name: Tool description integrity
controls.check: Review and version tool descriptions, prompts and schemas; quarantine unexpected changes before high-impact use.
controls.evidence: Alter a test description to include instructions and verify detection or containment.
controls.mistake: A server changes descriptive text and redirects how an already approved agent behaves.

controls.name: Server-initiated interactions
controls.check: Constrain sampling, elicitation, resource access and unsolicited requests; enforce consent, quotas and trust boundaries for supported features.
controls.evidence: Exercise a tool-triggered request outside the task's scope and retain decision records.
controls.mistake: The tool server induces model or user interactions that bypass the normal task gate.

name: Prompt injection and untrusted content
goal: Prevent untrusted instructions from gaining execution authority.

controls.name: All input channels covered
controls.check: Test direct prompts, documents, webpages, email, tickets, code comments, tool output, images, OCR and metadata as instruction carriers.
controls.evidence: Maintain a source-channel matrix and tests with synthetic adversarial markers.
controls.mistake: Defenses cover chat text while hidden HTML, OCR text or repository comments steer tools.

controls.name: Instruction-data separation
controls.check: Preserve source boundaries and provenance; keep policy enforcement external even when prompts instruct the model to ignore injected text.
controls.evidence: Inspect prompt assembly and verify prohibited actions remain blocked after injected instructions.
controls.mistake: Delimiter formatting or a stronger system prompt is treated as a complete security boundary.

controls.name: Tool-output distrust
controls.check: Treat tool results as untrusted data unless separately validated; prevent returned text from modifying policy or grants.
controls.evidence: Return an adversarial test result from a controlled tool and observe the next action decision.
controls.mistake: An authenticated tool is assumed to return authoritative operating instructions.

controls.name: Multi-turn and delayed injection
controls.check: Test instructions that activate after summarization, later turns, memory writes or particular events.
controls.evidence: Run staged benign tasks followed by trigger conditions; preserve full task lineage.
controls.mistake: A single-turn test misses an instruction planted for a future privileged task.

controls.name: Cross-agent injection
controls.check: Test whether a low-trust agent's summaries, plans or critiques can influence a privileged agent beyond the authorized task.
controls.evidence: Send a marked lower-trust summary into a protected workflow; verify downstream action denial.
controls.mistake: Peer-agent output is elevated to system-level trust merely because it is internal.

controls.name: Output-to-code boundaries
controls.check: Apply safe interpreters, parameterized operations and restricted execution when generated text becomes code, queries or templates.
controls.evidence: Test malicious synthetic content at the parser or executor; inspect actual calls and errors.
controls.mistake: The model refuses a dangerous request but generated output is still executed by another component.

controls.name: Defense evaluation quality
controls.check: Evaluate action-level outcomes, unsafe attempts and leakage across languages, encodings and realistic contexts; record limitations.
controls.evidence: Keep versioned test sets, repetitions, allowed controls and downstream ground truth.
controls.mistake: A refusal rate or classifier score hides successful side effects in background tools.

controls.name: No self-authorized remediation
controls.check: Prevent agents from changing their own guardrails, logging, identities or approvals in response to a claimed incident.
controls.evidence: Submit a synthetic emergency instruction and confirm only designated responders can change controls.
controls.mistake: Injected urgency persuades the agent to disable safeguards to fix the problem.

name: RAG, retrieval and knowledge integrity
goal: Retrieval relevance must never substitute for access control or source integrity.

controls.name: Authorization before retrieval
controls.check: Apply authenticated user and tenant scope to retrieval; independently check access before content enters context.
controls.evidence: Query another tenant's distinctive canary through normal and direct retrieval routes.
controls.mistake: Unauthorized chunks are retrieved first and removed only after the model has seen them.

controls.name: Controlled ingestion
controls.check: Authenticate source owners, validate imports, restrict write permissions and quarantine unknown or changed sources.
controls.evidence: Attempt unapproved ingestion and inspect source registry, approvals and ingestion audit trail.
controls.mistake: Anyone who can update a shared document can silently change high-trust operating context.

controls.name: Source and chunk lineage
controls.check: Preserve document version, chunk identifier, source URL or path, timestamps, ACL and content digest for every retrieved passage.
controls.evidence: Reconstruct one answer's exact authorized passages from retained versions and retrieval records.
controls.mistake: A citation names a document but cannot identify the text version used during execution.

controls.name: Poisoning-resistant promotion
controls.check: Review changes to high-impact knowledge, separate facts from instructions and verify authoritative claims independently.
controls.evidence: Use a synthetic poisoned document in a staging index; inspect promotion and action behavior.
controls.mistake: Repeated or highly ranked text is treated as verified policy because it appears in search results.

controls.name: Filters and reranking
controls.check: Maintain tenant and entitlement boundaries across hybrid search, graph expansion, reranking, deduplication and fallback search.
controls.evidence: Test restrictive queries through each retrieval mode and verify candidate-set scope.
controls.mistake: The vector search filters correctly but reranking or lexical fallback reintroduces restricted material.

controls.name: Index deletion and freshness
controls.check: Propagate source deletion, ACL change and correction to indexes, caches and derived summaries within a documented time.
controls.evidence: Remove a test document and revoke access; measure disappearance from all retrieval paths.
controls.mistake: Deleting the source leaves retrievable embeddings, cached chunks and generated summaries.

controls.name: Embedding and export protection
controls.check: Treat indexes, embeddings, snapshots and retrieval logs as potentially sensitive; limit exports and bulk similarity access.
controls.evidence: Inspect data-store permissions and test unauthorized snapshot or query access.
controls.mistake: Embeddings are assumed anonymous and distributed without the source's confidentiality controls.

controls.name: Retrieval confidence handling
controls.check: Distinguish relevance, source credibility and authorization; require independent evidence for high-impact conclusions.
controls.evidence: Review a conflicting-source task and observe escalation or bounded response.
controls.mistake: A high similarity score becomes a justification for a privileged infrastructure change.

name: Memory, shared state and persistence
goal: Prevent one task from silently rewriting the authority or behavior of later tasks.

controls.name: Memory scope isolation
controls.check: Partition working memory, long-term memory, cache and conversation state by authenticated tenant, user and workflow where required.
controls.evidence: Create distinct synthetic memories and test cross-scope retrieval and writes.
controls.mistake: A global agent memory leaks one customer's secrets or instructions into another task.

controls.name: Memory write authorization
controls.check: Define which agents may create, modify or delete memory and which sources may influence durable facts.
controls.evidence: Submit a lower-trust memory-write request and inspect server-side enforcement.
controls.mistake: Any tool result can add persistent instructions that future agents treat as trusted.

controls.name: Provenance and expiry
controls.check: Store origin, trust level, timestamp, validity, version and review status for remembered facts and instructions.
controls.evidence: Inspect a recalled fact and verify the original evidence and expiry behavior.
controls.mistake: An old incident workaround remains active months after its authority has expired.

controls.name: Authority separation in memory
controls.check: Do not store enforceable permissions or approvals as free-form remembered text; keep grants in a protected control plane.
controls.evidence: Plant a remembered claim of administrator approval and verify denial at execution.
controls.mistake: Memory says user approved earlier and substitutes for a current validated grant.

controls.name: Checkpoint and resume safety
controls.check: Validate resumed identity, policy version, expiry and resource scope; reauthorize pending effects after suspension.
controls.evidence: Resume a checkpoint after revocation or policy change; verify prohibited calls stop.
controls.mistake: An approved plan retains stale authority when restored into a different environment.

controls.name: Concurrent state integrity
controls.check: Control concurrent edits, ownership, version conflicts and atomic updates across agent branches.
controls.evidence: Exercise two branches modifying the same task state; retain conflict decisions and final state.
controls.mistake: One branch overwrites a denial or safe plan with an older permissive version.

controls.name: Poisoned state recovery
controls.check: Identify, quarantine and restore corrupted memories, summaries, indexes and caches with source-specific lineage.
controls.evidence: Seed a benign corruption marker and demonstrate removal from primary and derived state.
controls.mistake: Deleting the initial message leaves its transformed instructions in persistent summaries.

controls.name: Backups and retention
controls.check: Protect memory backups and debug dumps; apply documented retention and access rules to restored data.
controls.evidence: Review restore permissions and test whether expired or deleted synthetic data reappears.
controls.mistake: A clean live memory is re-poisoned or repopulated with sensitive data during restoration.

name: Data privacy, egress and confidentiality
owner: Data owner + privacy lead + network security
goal: Control where sensitive data can flow, including indirect and tool-mediated exports.

controls.name: Data classification
controls.check: Classify documents, fields, secrets, embeddings and trace artifacts; define allowed agent, provider and tool access.
controls.evidence: Trace representative sensitive fields through ingestion, context, output and storage.
controls.mistake: Only original documents are classified while derived summaries and traces are unrestricted.

controls.name: Provider data handling
controls.check: Record model and tool provider retention, training-use settings, regions, subprocessors and available deletion controls.
controls.evidence: Compare deployed settings and agreements with the data owner's requirements.
controls.mistake: A secure internal agent sends regulated data to an unapproved external inference service.

controls.name: Destination authorization
controls.check: Enforce approved domains, recipients, buckets, repositories and callback destinations before outbound effects.
controls.evidence: Use synthetic data and an unapproved destination; verify denial at the egress or tool boundary.
controls.mistake: An export is allowed because the tool is approved even though its destination is not.

controls.name: Indirect exfiltration paths
controls.check: Review URLs, query strings, images, telemetry, DNS, error reports, filenames, comments and browser uploads for data leakage.
controls.evidence: Send distinct canary markers through each suspected channel and inspect network evidence.
controls.mistake: Response DLP passes while data is embedded in a tool URL or analytics request.

controls.name: Output and trace minimization
controls.check: Redact credentials and unnecessary personal data before normal logs and exports; preserve restricted evidence separately when needed.
controls.evidence: Inspect representative traces and failure logs; test canary detection and role-based access.
controls.mistake: Verbose debugging collects complete prompts, headers and secrets in a widely accessible system.

controls.name: Tenant-specific export checks
controls.check: Apply source entitlement and destination entitlement to exports, attachments and shared artifacts.
controls.evidence: Attempt a legitimate export containing one unauthorized tenant's canary; inspect rejection.
controls.mistake: The user may invoke the export tool but is not authorized to export every selected record.

controls.name: Aggregated disclosure controls
controls.check: Review cumulative access, bulk extraction and repeated small queries; constrain combined disclosure over a workflow.
controls.evidence: Run bounded repeated queries in staging and verify aggregate limits and alerting.
controls.mistake: Per-call limits pass while many agents collectively reconstruct an entire sensitive dataset.

controls.name: Deletion across derivatives
controls.check: Track and remove authorized deletion targets from context caches, memory, traces, indexes and provider stores where supported.
controls.evidence: Use a synthetic record with known derivatives; document removal, retention exceptions and residuals.
controls.mistake: A deletion promise covers the primary database while copies persist elsewhere.

name: Runtime, browser and code execution
goal: Limit the local capabilities of coding, browsing and terminal agents.

controls.name: Runtime sandbox
controls.check: Isolate task execution with constrained filesystem, process, network and privilege access appropriate to risk.
controls.evidence: Run negative tests for forbidden paths, host access and process actions in disposable environments.
controls.mistake: A tool sandbox exists but helper commands execute directly on the host.

controls.name: Safe filesystem boundaries
controls.check: Canonicalize paths and constrain reads, writes, symlinks, archive extraction and generated artifact locations.
controls.evidence: Test boundary escapes with harmless files and inspect resolved paths and permissions.
controls.mistake: A permitted project path reaches secrets through a symlink or archive member.

controls.name: Shell and interpreter controls
controls.check: Prefer constrained operations over unrestricted shells; validate arguments and isolate permitted arbitrary code execution.
controls.evidence: Review executors and try forbidden synthetic commands, substitutions and interpreter access.
controls.mistake: An allowlisted executable accepts flags or scripts that enable broader command execution.

controls.name: Browser identity isolation
controls.check: Use task-specific browser profiles and scoped sessions; separate personal, corporate, tenant and administrative logins.
controls.evidence: Inspect cookies, saved credentials, extensions and session reuse across representative tasks.
controls.mistake: A browsing agent inherits an administrator's active session from a desktop profile.

controls.name: Browser action controls
controls.check: Constrain navigation, downloads, uploads, clipboard access and form submissions by task scope and destination.
controls.evidence: Test an unauthorized upload or submission with synthetic data and inspect effect logs.
controls.mistake: A read-oriented browser task submits data using a session with write permissions.

controls.name: Generated code distrust
controls.check: Treat generated scripts, SQL, templates and configuration as untrusted until checked and run in the intended boundary.
controls.evidence: Verify static checks, parameterization and staging execution before promotion.
controls.mistake: Code is considered safe because the same agent generated and reviewed it.

controls.name: Runtime cleanup
controls.check: Remove temporary files, cached credentials, downloads, mounted workspaces and spawned processes between tasks.
controls.evidence: Inspect a second task for previous-task canaries and active background processes.
controls.mistake: The visible task ends while a daemon, token file or browser session survives.

controls.name: Host sensor coverage
controls.check: Correlate process, file, network and container events with agent task and tool invocation identifiers.
controls.evidence: Run a harmless executable or file marker and reconstruct it in endpoint telemetry.
controls.mistake: Only chat and framework traces exist; native execution has no independent evidence.

name: Cloud, containers and network boundaries
goal: Prevent tool compromise from becoming control-plane or infrastructure compromise.

controls.name: Network segmentation
controls.check: Limit connectivity among agents, tools, databases and management endpoints; enforce least required east-west and egress access.
controls.evidence: Test approved and forbidden connections from the actual workload network namespace.
controls.mistake: Internet egress is filtered but internal administrator services remain reachable.

controls.name: Metadata and identity endpoints
controls.check: Restrict access to instance metadata, workload token endpoints and local credential services except for explicitly required components.
controls.evidence: Use safe connectivity tests and inspect identity endpoint policies and access logs.
controls.mistake: An agent-controlled fetch retrieves stronger cloud credentials from local metadata.

controls.name: Container privilege limits
controls.check: Avoid privileged mode, host mounts, exposed runtime sockets and unnecessary kernel capabilities; constrain service accounts.
controls.evidence: Review manifests and effective runtime settings; test harmless host-access negative cases.
controls.mistake: A non-root container can still control the host through a mounted Docker socket.

controls.name: Cluster authorization
controls.check: Limit Kubernetes and orchestration permissions by resource, namespace and action; separate deployment and task identities.
controls.evidence: Inspect effective RBAC and test denial for secret reads, exec and role creation.
controls.mistake: An agent with deployment rights can mount secrets or launch a more privileged pod.

controls.name: Protected management plane
controls.check: Keep IAM, policy administration, logging controls and emergency switches outside normal agent reach.
controls.evidence: Attempt restricted management operations with task identities; preserve denials.
controls.mistake: An agent can disable the audit trail or modify the containment mechanism.

controls.name: SSRF-resistant fetches
controls.check: Validate destinations, DNS resolution and redirect hops; block forbidden internal ranges and enforce network policy.
controls.evidence: Use a controlled redirect and internal test endpoint; verify forbidden access is denied.
controls.mistake: Initial URL validation passes but a redirect or resolution change reaches an internal service.

controls.name: Environment and tenant isolation
controls.check: Use distinct identities, secrets, network routes and resource boundaries for development, staging, production and tenants.
controls.evidence: Exercise cross-environment access from staging without exposing real production data.
controls.mistake: A staging agent can assume a production role because the federation trust is broad.

controls.name: Infrastructure state protection
controls.check: Version configurations, preserve audit trails and protect backups or state stores from agent-controlled deletion.
controls.evidence: Review storage and logging permissions; demonstrate recovery from a harmless configuration change.
controls.mistake: The same identity can change infrastructure and erase the evidence and rollback state.

name: Supply chain, models, plugins and skills
owner: Software supply chain lead + AI platform owner
goal: Treat every executable, instruction bundle and model artifact as a changeable dependency.

controls.name: Dependency inventory
controls.check: Track frameworks, SDKs, MCP servers, plugins, skills, prompts, model files, embeddings and container images with owners and versions.
controls.evidence: Reconcile builds and runtime dependencies with a component inventory and lockfiles.
controls.mistake: Only Python packages are inventoried; instruction bundles and tool servers are omitted.

controls.name: Artifact integrity
controls.check: Pin and verify approved artifact digests, signatures or provenance where available; retain the exact deployed versions.
controls.evidence: Compare running artifacts against release manifests and test rejection of altered packages.
controls.mistake: An image tag or model alias changes silently while the recorded version appears unchanged.

controls.name: Unsafe artifact loading
controls.check: Avoid unsafe deserialization and arbitrary remote code unless explicitly reviewed and isolated; inspect model loaders and import hooks.
controls.evidence: Test a harmless unapproved loader artifact in staging and verify rejection or sandboxing.
controls.mistake: A model download executes code before application-level agent controls are active.

controls.name: Skill and prompt permissions
controls.check: Review instruction packages for tool access, file reads, network effects and changes to approval behavior.
controls.evidence: Diff a skill update and test whether new requested capabilities require review.
controls.mistake: A harmless-looking skill update grants implicit permission to send data or modify systems.

controls.name: Registry and name trust
controls.check: Verify publishers, server names, package sources and installation commands; mitigate lookalike packages and tools.
controls.evidence: Test a synthetic unapproved publisher or ambiguous tool name in a private registry.
controls.mistake: A familiar name substitutes for verification of publisher and package integrity.

controls.name: Update review and rollout
controls.check: Stage dependency, model and tool updates with regression tests, risk review and controlled rollout; maintain rollback artifacts.
controls.evidence: Show a recent update's evidence and a rollback rehearsal using pinned artifacts.
controls.mistake: Automatic updates modify agent behavior or permissions directly in production.

controls.name: Provider outage and compromise
controls.check: Plan revocation, isolation, fallback and evidence access for a compromised model endpoint or tool supplier.
controls.evidence: Run a tabletop or isolated provider-blocking test and assess fallback permissions.
controls.mistake: Failover routes tasks to a provider with weaker data handling or broader credentials.

controls.name: Supply chain incident linkage
controls.check: Record component versions in task traces and link vulnerabilities or compromise indicators to affected executions.
controls.evidence: Query which tasks used a simulated affected version and identify downstream artifacts.
controls.mistake: An affected package is known, but historical task usage and generated outputs cannot be determined.

name: Development, MLOps and CI/CD
goal: Keep build, evaluation, deployment and data pipelines from becoming escalation routes.

controls.name: Protected repositories
controls.check: Enforce review and branch controls on agent code, prompts, tools, policy and deployment configuration; separate write from approval.
controls.evidence: Verify a test agent cannot merge or bypass protections using its normal credentials.
controls.mistake: The agent reviews and approves its own code using another shared identity.

controls.name: CI identity boundaries
controls.check: Scope build and deployment credentials by repository, environment and action; avoid secrets in untrusted pull-request jobs.
controls.evidence: Run a controlled fork or untrusted-change build and confirm no privileged secrets are exposed.
controls.mistake: A code-writing agent can trigger a pipeline that executes attacker-controlled code with production credentials.

controls.name: Evaluation isolation
controls.check: Run adversarial datasets, notebooks, fixtures and sample tools in isolated environments without production credentials.
controls.evidence: Inspect evaluation runners and verify restricted data and network access.
controls.mistake: Security tests contain hostile instructions but run inside a broadly privileged development environment.

controls.name: Training data integrity
controls.check: Track dataset source, authorization, transforms, review and version; protect fine-tuning and labeling pipelines from unauthorized edits.
controls.evidence: Introduce a benign test change and verify lineage, review and rejection controls.
controls.mistake: External support tickets become training examples without checking embedded adversarial instructions.

controls.name: Model promotion gates
controls.check: Validate security, privacy and action behavior for new base models, adapters and fine-tuned variants before release.
controls.evidence: Retain versioned evaluation results and deployment approval for a model change.
controls.mistake: A quality benchmark improvement is treated as proof that tool behavior remains safe.

controls.name: Deployment authorization
controls.check: Bind approved artifacts and deployment parameters to environment-specific grants; prevent agent-proposed changes from self-promoting.
controls.evidence: Try changed image digests, destinations and infrastructure parameters after approval.
controls.mistake: A safe diff is approved, but a different artifact is deployed under the same approval.

controls.name: Pipeline artifact protection
controls.check: Protect model registries, build caches, package indexes, signing keys, generated configuration and infrastructure state.
controls.evidence: Review write permissions and test unapproved artifact replacement with synthetic packages.
controls.mistake: A low-privilege agent poisons a cache consumed by a privileged release job.

controls.name: Release and rollback lineage
controls.check: Record code, model, prompt, tool, policy and dataset versions as one deployed configuration; keep a verified rollback target.
controls.evidence: Reconstruct a historical release and restore it in staging with current security controls.
controls.mistake: Rollback restores vulnerable prompts or grants together with the desired application version.

name: Approvals and high-impact actions
goal: Make human approval specific, verifiable and independent of agent-controlled presentation.

controls.name: Risk-based approval scope
controls.check: Define approval requirements for IAM changes, production writes, deletion, money movement, external sharing and irreversible actions.
controls.evidence: Map each high-impact tool operation to an enforceable approval rule and accountable approver.
controls.mistake: Approval covers tool access in general rather than the risky operation and target.

controls.name: Canonical action presentation
controls.check: Show exact action, target, arguments, data destination, diff and expected impact using trusted rendering.
controls.evidence: Compare approval UI details with canonical executor input for a representative task.
controls.mistake: The agent's reassuring summary hides dangerous parameters or additional side effects.

controls.name: Bound approval to payload
controls.check: Bind approval to a canonical request digest, identity, resource, expiry and relevant state; invalidate it after material changes.
controls.evidence: Change one approved argument or target and confirm execution requires a new approval.
controls.mistake: The executor accepts an old approval after the agent changes the command.

controls.name: Independent approver identity
controls.check: Authenticate approvers and enforce role or separation requirements; prevent agent or requester self-approval when prohibited.
controls.evidence: Test wrong-role and self-approval cases and inspect identity records.
controls.mistake: An agent-controlled callback or account is accepted as an authorized human decision.

controls.name: Single-use and expiry
controls.check: Define approval lifetime and use count; reject replay, stale approvals and resumed tasks outside the approved window.
controls.evidence: Replay a test approval and execute after expiry; verify safe denial.
controls.mistake: One approval becomes a permanent permission for repeated operations.

controls.name: State-aware execution
controls.check: Revalidate authorization and relevant resource state just before effect; detect time-of-check/time-of-use changes.
controls.evidence: Change target state after review and confirm the executor rechecks or requests fresh approval.
controls.mistake: An approved operation applies to a materially different object when execution eventually runs.

controls.name: Honest rejection behavior
controls.check: On denial or timeout, stop the protected effect; prohibit alternate tools, repeated persuasion or background retries to bypass approval.
controls.evidence: Deny a controlled task and inspect every branch, queue and tool route.
controls.mistake: The front end reports cancellation while a delegate completes the action anyway.

controls.name: Emergency authority
controls.check: Define controlled break-glass identities, exact scope, duration, logging and review; keep them outside normal agent control.
controls.evidence: Exercise emergency activation and expiry with responsible humans and retained evidence.
controls.mistake: The agent interprets urgency as permission to activate administrator access.

name: Autonomy, resource limits and business integrity
goal: Bound total effects and cost while preserving safe business behavior.

controls.name: Explicit autonomy levels
controls.check: Define observe, recommend, draft, approved-execute and autonomous-execute modes with per-action policy.
controls.evidence: Verify deployed mode and attempt an operation from the next-higher mode.
controls.mistake: A product toggle says assistive while its tool identity can act autonomously.

controls.name: Global task budgets
controls.check: Limit aggregate tokens, time, money, tool calls, spawned tasks and compute across delegates and retries.
controls.evidence: Exercise controlled fan-out and verify one shared budget and clear termination reason.
controls.mistake: Local limits reset for each child agent, creating an unbounded combined workflow.

controls.name: Business transaction constraints
controls.check: Enforce amounts, counterparties, schedules, entitlements and other domain invariants in trusted services.
controls.evidence: Try validly formatted transactions outside business limits using synthetic accounts.
controls.mistake: A schema-valid transaction is harmful because business constraints were left to the model.

controls.name: Idempotent effects
controls.check: Use idempotency keys and deduplication for payments, deployment, notifications and other non-repeatable actions.
controls.evidence: Simulate timeouts and duplicate deliveries; confirm exactly the intended number of side effects.
controls.mistake: The agent retries after an ambiguous response and repeats a successful transaction.

controls.name: Planning versus execution
controls.check: Separate a proposed plan from an authorized executable operation; recheck each concrete action when plans evolve.
controls.evidence: Compare plan approval with actual tool effects and test an added step.
controls.mistake: Approving a broad plan implicitly authorizes every subsequently invented action.

controls.name: Loop and retry controls
controls.check: Bound recursion, escalation, retries and re-planning; handle repeated authorization failures as stops or explicit escalation.
controls.evidence: Trigger a persistent harmless error and measure attempts and termination across workers.
controls.mistake: The agent changes tools repeatedly until one route bypasses the initial restriction.

controls.name: High-impact action rate limits
controls.check: Set aggregate per-principal, workflow, tenant and target limits with burst controls and a circuit breaker.
controls.evidence: Run synthetic rapid actions and verify throttling, alerting and final resource state.
controls.mistake: A per-agent limit misses coordinated writes by many delegated agents.

controls.name: Safe degraded operation
controls.check: Document read-only or paused modes for failures, low-confidence decisions and missing evidence; test recovery transitions.
controls.evidence: Simulate an unavailable dependency and inspect resulting permissions and queued work.
controls.mistake: An automatic fallback agent has greater privilege than the failed primary workflow.

name: Logging, tracing and forensic readiness
goal: Record independently verifiable facts that explain authorization and actual effects.

controls.name: Stable correlation identifiers
controls.check: Record tenant, task, trace, span, parent span, delegation, tool invocation and external request IDs across all hops.
controls.evidence: Reconstruct a multi-agent task using those IDs without relying on narrative summaries.
controls.mistake: Framework traces end at a tool boundary and cannot join to cloud or database audit logs.

controls.name: Identity and authorization evidence
controls.check: Log origin, delegator, executing principal, requested scope, effective scope, policy version, decision and reason.
controls.evidence: Inspect allowed and denied calls, including service-owned delegation and direct resource access.
controls.mistake: Logs show a service account but omit the principal and authorization that caused it to act.

controls.name: Input and source lineage
controls.check: Record source identifiers, trust classification, content digests and protected evidence references for relevant inputs.
controls.evidence: Retrieve a controlled task's exact source version with authorized forensic access.
controls.mistake: A URL is recorded, but the mutable page no longer contains the triggering content.

controls.name: Tool effects and outcomes
controls.check: Record canonical arguments or protected references, destination, result, error, retries and independent effect confirmation.
controls.evidence: Compare tool records with resource before/after state and resource-side request IDs.
controls.mistake: The model says action completed while execution failed, or claims failure after a successful effect.

controls.name: Versioned runtime configuration
controls.check: Capture model, prompt, agent, tool, skill, code, policy and deployment versions in each task's evidence.
controls.evidence: Reconstruct the precise deployed configuration of a historical task.
controls.mistake: A generic model name or tool alias cannot identify the version that ran.

controls.name: Protected trace collection
controls.check: Use access-controlled, tamper-evident central collection with retention and integrity checks; separate agent and collector privileges.
controls.evidence: Attempt log deletion with agent credentials and test loss detection and protected export.
controls.mistake: A compromised agent can edit or delete the only trace used for investigation.

controls.name: Time and completeness
controls.check: Synchronize clocks, record event and receipt times, detect dropped spans and preserve high-risk events without unsafe sampling.
controls.evidence: Simulate delayed and lost events; verify alerts and a documented timeline uncertainty.
controls.mistake: Sampled traces make a privileged branch disappear while clocks imply the wrong order.

controls.name: Evidence export and custody
controls.check: Prepare restricted export, hashing, custody records, retention holds and redacted sharing for incident evidence.
controls.evidence: Export a test incident and verify access, integrity and handover records.
controls.mistake: Responders export full traces into an unprotected workspace or cannot obtain vendor-held evidence.

name: Detection engineering and triage
goal: Detect suspicious chains, distinguish attempts from effects, and route actionable alerts.

controls.name: Cross-agent escalation detection
controls.check: Alert on unusual low-trust-to-high-privilege delegations, denied scope expansion and high-impact actions lacking expected origin grants.
controls.evidence: Exercise a controlled escalation attempt and correlate handoff, policy and tool events.
controls.mistake: Only direct privilege escalation is monitored; legitimate service calls hide delegated abuse.

controls.name: Unexpected action sequences
controls.check: Baseline task types and detect new tools, destinations, targets, role assumptions, mass writes and log-control changes.
controls.evidence: Run a synthetic out-of-pattern sequence; review alert context and false-positive handling.
controls.mistake: Every individual call is normal, but their sequence produces an unauthorized outcome.

controls.name: Injection-linked effects
controls.check: Correlate suspicious source content or trust-boundary violations with concrete tool actions rather than relying only on text classifiers.
controls.evidence: Use a canary injection task and compare attempted and completed downstream effects.
controls.mistake: An injection detector fires but nobody checks whether infrastructure was already changed.

controls.name: Leakage and egress detection
controls.check: Monitor classified canaries, unusual exports, destinations, data volumes and sensitive content in tool calls and telemetry.
controls.evidence: Use synthetic sensitive markers with a controlled endpoint and validate receipt and alerting.
controls.mistake: Chat output is clean while data leaves through a browser, webhook or trace provider.

controls.name: Persistence and drift detection
controls.check: Alert on memory, knowledge, tool description, skill, policy, IAM and deployment changes that affect future behavior.
controls.evidence: Modify a test artifact and verify attribution, version diff and ownership notification.
controls.mistake: The incident remains dormant in persistent state after the initial process is stopped.

controls.name: Identity abuse correlation
controls.check: Correlate agent activity with credential use outside expected workloads, regions, audiences and task contexts.
controls.evidence: Use an isolated test token from an unexpected client and verify investigation context.
controls.mistake: Credential theft is dismissed because the service account often performs automated activity.

controls.name: Operational alert ownership
controls.check: Assign severity, queue, responder, escalation route and evidence links; test delivery outside normal business hours.
controls.evidence: Run a test alert through acknowledgment and escalation; measure response against local objectives.
controls.mistake: A dashboard indicator exists, but no person is responsible for acting on it.

controls.name: Impact-based triage
controls.check: Separate injection attempt, blocked execution, unauthorized action, data exposure and infrastructure takeover; record evidence and uncertainty.
controls.evidence: Triage representative cases using resource logs and business-owner validation.
controls.mistake: A model's narrative or refusal is treated as sufficient proof of compromise or safety.

name: Containment readiness
goal: Stop new and pending effects without relying on the compromised agent to cooperate.

controls.name: Out-of-band kill controls
controls.check: Provide trusted controls to suspend workflows, tool access and privileged execution by agent, tenant, identity or platform.
controls.evidence: Trigger a staging kill switch from an independent responder identity and measure stop latency.
controls.mistake: The kill switch sends a prompt to the agent instead of enforcing execution denial.

controls.name: Granular delegation blocking
controls.check: Allow responders to disable a dangerous handoff or receiver while retaining safe observation where appropriate.
controls.evidence: Block a test low-to-high privilege edge and verify all alternate delegation routes.
controls.mistake: Disabling the visible agent leaves the privileged delegate directly accessible.

controls.name: Queue and scheduler containment
controls.check: Pause or cancel queued tasks, retries, cron jobs, callbacks and child tasks; record in-flight operations and cancellation limits.
controls.evidence: Suspend a workflow with pending tasks and check actual worker and resource behavior.
controls.mistake: New chat requests stop, but queued writes continue using already obtained authority.

controls.name: Credential and session containment
controls.check: Revoke or restrict compromised grants and sessions, block direct APIs where needed and track residual credential validity.
controls.evidence: Measure denial across active sessions, cached policy, refresh grants and downstream services.
controls.mistake: A service principal is disabled while already issued credentials remain usable.

controls.name: Egress and resource isolation
controls.check: Restrict outbound destinations, network access, tool routes and vulnerable resources using trusted infrastructure controls.
controls.evidence: Test isolation with synthetic data and verify legitimate emergency responder access remains usable.
controls.mistake: The workflow is paused, but an active process still exports data or changes resources.

controls.name: State quarantine
controls.check: Quarantine affected memory, retrieval sources, caches, checkpoints, descriptions and skill packages; prevent re-ingestion.
controls.evidence: Seed a benign persistence marker and confirm no resumed or alternate workflow can recall it.
controls.mistake: A clean restart reloads the same poisoned state immediately.

controls.name: Evidence-preserving containment
controls.check: Define which volatile evidence to capture and which effects demand immediate blocking; record actions, times and rationale.
controls.evidence: Exercise both a fast-moving harmful effect and a stable incident with evidence capture.
controls.mistake: Responders either delay critical containment for perfect evidence or destroy all evidence reflexively.

controls.name: Trusted emergency access
controls.check: Maintain tested responder identities and recovery channels that agents cannot alter; log their use and time-limit elevation.
controls.evidence: Test access during an IAM or control-plane outage with separated credentials.
controls.mistake: Responders depend on the compromised agent's tool account to contain the incident.

name: Investigation and blast-radius analysis
owner: DFIR lead + cloud + business system owners
goal: Reconstruct the causal chain and determine what actually changed or left the boundary.

controls.name: Causal chain reconstruction
controls.check: Trace untrusted source, Agent A, handoff, Agent B, policy decision, tool invocation and final effect with evidence at each boundary.
controls.evidence: Assemble a timeline using source versions, traces, identity records and resource audit logs.
controls.mistake: The first suspicious prompt is identified, but the authority escalation point remains unknown.

controls.name: Authority at incident time
controls.check: Reconstruct effective IAM, grants, policy, approvals and credential lifetimes as they existed during the incident.
controls.evidence: Preserve versioned policy and entitlement snapshots and join them to event timestamps.
controls.mistake: Investigators inspect today's permissions and assume they explain yesterday's execution.

controls.name: Resource-side ground truth
controls.check: Verify file, database, cloud, CI/CD and business changes independently of model statements; include partial failures and reversals.
controls.evidence: Compare audit logs and before/after state with tool outcomes and transaction records.
controls.mistake: The agent's explanation is treated as a trustworthy forensic account.

controls.name: Reachable versus exercised scope
controls.check: Separate potentially reachable assets from confirmed accessed or modified assets; document confidence and collection gaps.
controls.evidence: Build capability paths and evidence-backed affected-asset lists with explicit uncertainty.
controls.mistake: Broad permissions are reported as confirmed compromise of every resource they could reach.

controls.name: Data exposure determination
controls.check: Trace source data, transformations, destinations, receipts and retained copies; distinguish access, transmission and confirmed receipt.
controls.evidence: Use gateway, provider, endpoint and destination evidence; note missing or encrypted visibility.
controls.mistake: Any retrieval is labeled exfiltration, or lack of a chat leak is taken as proof of no exposure.

controls.name: Persistence and lateral movement
controls.check: Inspect new identities, grants, jobs, code, configuration, memories, knowledge entries and tool integrations across the chain.
controls.evidence: Compare trusted baselines with current state and search linked task and identity histories.
controls.mistake: The running agent is clean while a malicious job or shared memory remains active.

controls.name: Hypothesis and evidence discipline
controls.check: Track competing explanations, evidence reliability, timeline gaps and confirmation criteria; avoid inferring private model reasoning.
controls.evidence: Maintain a hypothesis log tied to reproducible facts and protected evidence references.
controls.mistake: Speculation about hidden reasoning substitutes for verifiable inputs, decisions and effects.

controls.name: Business impact validation
controls.check: Work with owners to validate operational, financial, customer and data impact, including duplicate or incomplete transactions.
controls.evidence: Reconcile affected transactions and systems against independent business records.
controls.mistake: The technical incident ends while corrupted records or unintended customer actions remain unresolved.

name: Recovery, assurance and exercises
goal: Restore trusted operation and prove that the unsafe path cannot simply recur.

controls.name: Trusted rebuild and restore
controls.check: Restore verified code, images, policies and state from known-good sources; validate backup integrity and retained malicious content.
controls.evidence: Rebuild a test environment and inspect identity, tool and state baselines before activation.
controls.mistake: A backup contains the same poisoned memory, vulnerable package or expanded grant.

controls.name: Re-establish bounded identities
controls.check: Issue clean scoped credentials through trusted components, remove unauthorized grants and prevent reissuance to quarantined workloads.
controls.evidence: Test old credentials, refresh paths and new identity scope after recovery.
controls.mistake: Recovery rotates secrets but preserves the authorization defect that enabled the incident.

controls.name: Correct causal control failure
controls.check: Fix the actual boundary failure in delegation, authorization, tool execution or state promotion; do not rely only on prompt edits.
controls.evidence: Repeat the original controlled scenario and variants at the resource boundary.
controls.mistake: A new system prompt appears to work once while the permissive execution route remains.

controls.name: Validate data and transaction repair
controls.check: Reconcile modified records, files, deployments and business effects; approve compensating actions through normal trusted controls.
controls.evidence: Use independent before/after comparisons and owner sign-off for repaired state.
controls.mistake: A rollback repairs infrastructure but leaves duplicate payments or corrupted customer data.

controls.name: Staged return to service
controls.check: Resume with restricted scope, enhanced monitoring and explicit exit criteria; review queued work before releasing it.
controls.evidence: Run a canary workload and verify policy, evidence and effects before increasing autonomy.
controls.mistake: Full autonomy resumes immediately and old queued tasks execute under new credentials.

controls.name: Regression and adversarial coverage
controls.check: Maintain reproducible tests for the original failure and adjacent paths across models, prompts, tools and asynchronous execution.
controls.evidence: Retain versioned expected outcomes and actual downstream evidence for every changed release.
controls.mistake: A single benign replay passes while another delegate or fallback reproduces the defect.

controls.name: Tabletop and technical drills
controls.check: Exercise responder decisions and real controls for identity, queue, egress, memory and recovery failures; include vendors.
controls.evidence: Record findings, measured containment latency and assigned corrective actions.
controls.mistake: A written playbook exists but its APIs, contacts and emergency permissions have never been tested.

controls.name: Lessons and readiness maintenance
controls.check: Update the checklist, detections, risk register, architecture and future playbooks after incidents and major changes.
controls.evidence: Track corrective actions to evidence-backed closure and reassess exceptions and gate status.
controls.mistake: Lessons are documented but never change production permissions, tests or responder capability.
